messages.subject: Re: How to plot time series of monthly values in ggplot
messages.subject_clean: How to plot time series of monthly values in ggplot
messages.body_plain:
No, you can keep year and month as separate columns and then use

ggplot(data, aes(x = interaction(month, year) y= value)

Op maandag 15 oktober 2018 06:39:01 UTC+2 schreef lily li:

> Thanks for your reply.
> I'm still not clear how to do it. Should I combine the year and month to year-month format first, such as 1993-01, 1993-02, etc?

> >
> > yes, as Shreya said. tidy it first please. you will need to use the function gather()
> >

> > On Fri, Oct 12, 2018 at 7:21 AM Shreya Agarwal <shrey...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > > Hi Lily,
> > >
> > > The dataset you're referring to is not tidy (vertical data). Once you have months as columns and all the values under another separate  column, you'll have clearly defined x-values and y-values. Hope that helps.
> > >
> > > To tidy the data: http://garrettgman.github.io/tidying/
> > > (scroll down to 'spread' and 'gather' part on the webpage shared above)
> > >
> > > Please let me know if you have any questions.
> > >
> > > Thanks,
> > > Shreya
> > >

> > > On Fri, Oct 12, 2018 at 10:06 AM lily li <choc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > > > Hi ggplot users,
> > > >
> > > > I have a dataset like this exactly.
> > > > http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com/file/n4162534/data.jpg
> > > >
> > > > How to draw time series of x-axis as monthly data, such as 1993-01, 1993-02, ..., 1993-12, 1994-01, ..., 1994-12, etc. Then y-axis as the values in ggplot2? I searched online, and one way seems to compile the dataset as 1993-01-01, 1993-02-01, etc, and then plot it as monthly values. But I see if there is a way to plot the monthly data directly? Thanks for any kind of help.

And here's the ggplot code including the fill variable:

# create custom palette with 'white' color for dummies, added 8 custom colors for data set
cols <- c("#fec44f", "#fc9272", "#a1d99b", "#fee0d2",
          "#2ca25f", "#8856a7", "#43a2ca", "#fdbb84",
          "#e34a33", "#a6bddb", "#dd1c77",
          "#4286f4","#2d5634","#a3a864","#626358",
          "#937e57","#918a7e","#877a64","#d18d68","#ffffff")

str(cols)

# plotting chart with 3 point font for labels
ggplot() +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values=cols) +
  geom_bar(data=alldata, aes(x=step, y=Users, fill=content), stat="identity", width=1) +
  geom_text(data=alldata[alldata$content!='dummy', ],
            aes(x=step, y=pos, label=paste0(content, '-', Users/1000, 'K')),
            size=18, color='white', fontface="bold") +
  geom_ribbon(data=fsa.lines, aes(x=step, ymax=max(maxx), ymin=maxx, group=1), fill='white') +
  geom_line(data=fsa.lines, aes(x=step, y=maxx, group=1), color='darkred', size=18) +
  geom_ribbon(data=fsa.lines, aes(x=step, ymax=minx, ymin=min(minx), group=1), fill='white') +
  geom_line(data=fsa.lines, aes(x=step, y=minx, group=1), color='darkred', size=18) +
  geom_text(data=step.rates, aes(x=step, y=(fsa.lines$minx[-1]), label=paste0(rate*100, '%')), hjust=1.2,
            color='darkblue', fontface="bold") +
  theme(legend.position='none', axis.ticks=element_blank(), axis.text.x=element_blank(),
        axis.title.x=element_blank())

The final plot should look similar to this:
